messages:
sara: quick q — running into inconsistent behavior for /v1/generate when clients don't send Accept header. Some responses return Content-Type: application/json + body with missing keys vs explicit nulls. Should we standardize on omitting absent optional fields? @tom

 tom: we decided earlier to prefer omission for optional primitives, but for structured outputs (objects/arrays) prefer empty object/array not null. See api-contract doc but agree it's fuzzy. :thinking:

 dev-bot: contract-checker CI — /v1/generate schema validation failed on canary: field 'choices[0].metadata' is null but schema expects object or absent.
```
ERROR: choices.0.metadata: null not allowed (object or missing)
```
 build: #5568

 liam: classic — we need deterministic client experience. For streaming clients, null breaks parsers. Proposal: update JSON schema to allow `null` only for top-level 'note' field, otherwise either omit or use {} / [].

 anika: +1 to avoiding nulls in arrays/objects. Quick compatibility plan: accept nulls from old models for 2 releases, but canonical output should omit. I'll open a PR to add post-processing sanitizer in runtime (replace null object -> {} ; null array -> []).

 sara: thanks. Can you also add an explicit Content-Type enforcement? Some clients rely on it. If missing, runtime should set application/json; charset=utf-8.

 tom: yep. Also add a lightweight lint in pre-merge that runs small sample through sanitizer. If sanitizer changes output, fail CI with note 'contract sanitizer altering response' so reviewers see.

 anika: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/compare/contract-sanitizer (draft). Added tests. cc @liam for schema tweak.

 liam: will review today. Note: update release notes under 'behavior changes' and make a canary with header enforcement turned off by default then flip after 1 week.

 sara: awesome. I'll coordinate with SDK folks to handle omitted fields gracefully. Thanks :thumbsup:
